text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the five activities A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 each appeared in roughly 18–25 in 100 traces, around 35% of the way through the trace, and virtually all of their outgoing transitions went to A28 (A19 to A28 in about 100 in 100 cases, A25 and A26 in about 97 in 100). In the later window they sit around 58–63% through the trace and lead to A30 or A34 instead (A19: about 56 in 100 to A30 and 38 to A34; A20 splits about 50/50; A25, A26 and A27 similarly). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

- A47 changed in the opposite direction: earlier its outgoing transitions were spread across the five activities (about 16–19 in 100 each), while in the later window about 91 in 100 go straight to A28; the position gap from A47 to A28 shrank from two steps (about 90 in 100 traces) to one step (about 91 in 100). [DIR008, LAG005]

- The order between the five activities and A28/A29 reversed: earlier each of the five ran before A28 and before A29 in essentially every trace where they co-occurred (e.g., A20 before A28 in about 20 in 100 traces, never after); in the later window A28 and A29 come first (A28 before A20 in about 22 in 100, A29 before A20 in about 22 in 100), and the same reversal holds for the pairs with A19, A25 and A27, while co-occurrence rates stayed similar. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]

- A step was inserted between A29 and A34: earlier A29→A30 and A30→A34 were immediately consecutive (gap of one step in about 99 in 100 traces; A29 reached A34 in two steps in about 97 in 100); in the later window two-step gaps appear about half the time and A29 reaches A34 three steps later in about 94 in 100 traces. A29 and A30 now also route into the five activities about 45–50 in 100 times, where previously they almost always went to A30, and A30 to A34. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, DIR006, DIR007]

- A28 and A29 still occur in every trace in both windows and moved only slightly earlier (A28 mean position about 0.38 to 0.36; A29 about 0.60 to 0.58). [POS006, POS007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block of five alternative activities — A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 — was relocated. In the earlier window, A47 branched to one of the five, which then led into A28, so the block sat between A47 and A28, before A28 and A29; in the later window the block sits after A29/A30 and before A34: the five activities now lead to A30 or A34, A29 and A30 route into them about half the time, and A47 connects directly to A28. This is shown directly by the successor changes for all five activities and A47, the order reversals in all eight pairs with A28/A29, the position shift from about 35% to about 60% of the trace, and the gap changes (A47→A28 from two steps to one; A29→A34 from two steps to three). With 28 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected by chance among 129 tested units, the pattern as a whole is unlikely to be a sampling artefact. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Limitations: the window samples cannot fully distinguish a genuine relocation of the block from the block being dropped at its old position while an equivalent block was inserted at the new one; the similar participation shares across windows (e.g., A27 in about 21 in 100 traces in both) are consistent with a move but do not prove it. The internal rule of the block — whether exactly one of the five runs per trace — is only implied by the gap data, not directly observed. One gap item on A47→A26 rests on only 2 after-window observations and was not relied upon. [LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Other differences: trace participation of the five activities shifted modestly (A19 down from about 25 to 17 in 100 traces; A25 up from about 18 to 24 in 100; the others roughly stable), which may be a side effect of the relocation or ordinary sampling variation. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
